physics.title: The physics of latency
physics.desc: In fiber, light covers 1 km every ~5 µs. Move the distance and compare it with the typical delay of other access technologies.
physics.note: Approximate reference. Fiber propagation is physics (≈ 5 µs/km). Typical access delays (FTTH ~2 ms, cable ~10 ms, 4G ~35 ms) are industry reference values and vary by network.

fiberType.title: Fiber type
fiberType.body: The type of glass decides how much light is lost per kilometer and at every bend in the cable.

wavelengths.title: Wavelengths
wavelengths.body: Download and upload travel on different colors of light through the same strand, without getting in each other's way.

redundancy.title: Redundancy
redundancy.body: The alternate routes that keep service up if a stretch of the network is cut.

router.title: Home equipment
router.body: The equipment decides how much of your speed reaches each room over Wi-Fi.

symmetry.title: Symmetry in light
symmetry.desc: Each flash is data travelling through the fiber: download toward your home and upload toward the network. Switch plans and compare a symmetrical connection with an asymmetrical one.

faq.lead: What people ask us most before signing up.

speed.q: Will I get the advertised speed?
speed.a: Each plan's speed is the maximum delivered to your home, the same down and up. Over a cable you get closest to that maximum; over Wi-Fi it depends on your device, distance and walls.

symmetric.a: You upload as fast as you download. Video calls, cloud backups, live streams and big files go up as fast as they come down.

install.q: How much does installation cost and how long does it take?
install.a: A technician brings the fiber to your house or apartment, installs the equipment and leaves everything working.

contract.q: Is there a minimum term? How do I cancel?

router.a: Yes. Every plan includes a modem on loan at no extra cost for as long as your service is active: a Wi-Fi 7 modem with {wifi7} and a Wi-Fi 6 modem with {wifi6}. Wi-Fi 7's top speed needs compatible devices; older devices still connect fine.

staticIp.q: Can I get a static IP?
